intro: Hospitality covers hotels, restaurants, and events, and it's one of the easier fields to enter with many roles requiring no experience. Positions span front desk, servers and hosts, housekeeping, and kitchen support, often with flexible shifts and, in tipped roles, extra take-home pay. The field suits outgoing, dependable people who enjoy fast-paced, customer-facing work, though there are behind-the-scenes roles too. Because hotels and restaurants operate every day, openings tend to be available year-round with extra demand in busy seasons. Here's an overview and where to find openings.

sections.h: What the work is really like day-to-day
sections.p: Hospitality is active and people-centered. Servers and hosts greet guests, take and deliver orders, and keep tables turning during busy rushes. Front-desk staff check guests in and out, answer questions, and handle requests. Housekeepers clean and reset a set number of rooms per shift. Kitchen and prep roles focus on food preparation and keeping the line moving. Most roles keep you on your feet and moving, and teamwork matters, especially during peak meal or check-in times.
Hospitality schedules are flexible because hotels and restaurants run early mornings through late nights.
